finding.title: Strip profile_id / child_profile_id from tutor_pin_service.dart and tutor_invite_use_cases.dart analytics events
finding.why: PV-1 explicitly bans profile_id and per-child identifiers as analytics parameters; the digest's baseline only excuses the three already-cited lines in lib/core/analytics/analytics_service.dart. These are different sites in a different file (tutor_pin_set fires with the tutor's own profile_id; tutor_invite_sent fires with the target child's child_profile_id), discovered while tracing the domain services my batch's screens call — the same class of per-user-identifier leak the rule was written to prevent, in a children's-learning-app analytics stream that PV-3/PV-4 assume is otherwise minimized.
finding.recommendation: Drop profile_id/child_profile_id/grant_id from these logEvent calls, or replace with an opaque, non-correlatable value if event-level de-duplication is genuinely needed. Extend the Rule-0 checker for PV-1 from analytics_service.dart-only to a repo-wide grep over all logEvent(...) parameters: {...} call sites for the banned key list.
acceptance_criteria: tutor_pin_set and tutor_invite_sent/accepted/declined events no longer carry profile_id/child_profile_id/grant_id in parameters

a grep-based checker scans all lib/**/*.dart logEvent(...) parameter maps for banned keys (profile_id, child_profile_id, sefaria_ref, grant_id) repo-wide and fails non-zero on a hit, extending the existing analytics_service.dart-scoped check
